analyzed_vuln.description: The PoV triggers a double-free because the fuzzer creates one KV pair in `prop` and then runs two iterations with different config maps. In the first iteration (`config_map_mult`), `flb_config_map_set()` stores/aliases the KV value SDS into a MULT string map entry, and `flb_config_map_destroy()` frees that SDS via `destroy_map_val()` (FLB_CONFIG_MAP_STR path). After that, the same `prop` list is still released with `flb_kv_release()`, which frees the same SDS again from the KV item. Root cause is ownership misuse in the harness: the same allocated property value is handed to config-map machinery that frees it, then freed again as KV-owned memory.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Use harness `flb-it-fuzz-config_map_fuzzer_OSSFUZZ` with input that makes the property key match a MULT string config entry (e.g., `mult_string`) so map set/destroy processes it as FLB_CONFIG_MAP_STR MULT. Data flow: input -> `get_null_terminated()` -> `flb_kv_item_create(&prop, key, val)` allocates SDS -> `flb_config_map_set(&prop, map, &ctx)` attaches value into map -> `flb_config_map_destroy(map)` frees it -> `flb_kv_release(&prop)` frees same pointer again. The crash occurs even with minimal/empty-ish value content once key selection causes this ownership overlap.
